name: Goddess of Whim (Retro Formats)
desc: Toss a coin and call Heads or Tails. Call it right and this card's ATK will be doubled during this turn. Call it wrong and it will be halved during this turn.

cdb_provenance.detail: type, atk, def, level, race, attribute and setcode are copied from the row for the modern card (67959180) in cards.cdb at the ignis-babelcdb revision pinned in data/sources.json. They are NOT independently checked against a period printing: a stat change between the period card and the modern one would not be reproduced. category (a client search filter, not gameplay) is left 0 rather than copied. ot is 8 (SCOPE_ILLEGAL) as for every historical-implementation row upstream.

authorship.note: Adapted from Project Ignis's script for the modern card, official/c67959180.lua at the ignis-cardscripts pin, by applying only the period difference the erratum record states (the summary above) and pointing the effect description at the modern card's strings, because this generated row carries none. It is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later like its upstream (LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-or-later.txt); the rest of this repository stays MIT. Round 031 labelled it original, written without opening any Project Ignis card script; round 031's review measured that version as too close to this upstream file to be independent, and the owner decided on 2026-09-27 that such scripts are credited, labelled derived and kept under the upstream's licence. Round 032 rebased it on the upstream file itself.

not_reproduced: The record's sources establish that the period text carries no use limit (the 2012 erratum added "Once per turn"). They do not say how period rulings treated a second activation in the same turn while the first is still resolving or with other effects in play; the script has no limit at all, and a further activation is offered whenever the engine's ordinary rules offer an Ignition effect.

Halving is the upstream script's c:GetAttack()/2; how the engine rounds half of an odd ATK is not something the record's sources state, and the ATK values after a toss are not tested (the outcome of the coin is random); only that the effect can be activated again is.
The ATK change is a final-ATK setting applied at resolution to the ATK the card has at that moment; how it combines with other ATK-changing effects is not modelled or tested.
The call is made by the controller before the toss, as the engine's Duel.CallCoin does; the record's sources do not describe how the period rules ordered the call and the toss.
The card row's statline is copied from the modern row and not checked against the period printing.

rulings_check.difference: The effect has no use limit, so it can be activated again in the same turn; the modern card is "Once per turn".
